use-sounds-in-a-mini-exchange.label: Use Sounds in a Mini Exchange
use-sounds-in-a-mini-exchange.summary: Use the first Kreyòl sound-spelling anchors in a tiny exchange, combining listening, speaking, building, and writing before the module review.

exchange-choice-response.title: Recognize the greeting
exchange-choice-response.prompt: Which Kreyòl word can open the tiny exchange practiced in this lesson?
exchange-choice-response.hint: Look for the spelling feature practiced in this lesson.

help.concept: Kreyòl spelling keeps meaningful vowel and sound patterns visible in the written word.
help.hint_1: Focus on the spelling pattern named in the lesson instead of applying English spelling habits.
help.hint_2: Compare the letters and accent marks carefully before choosing your response.

exchange-fill-mesi.title: Complete the thank-you word
exchange-fill-mesi.prompt: Choose the spelling that completes mèsi.
exchange-fill-mesi.hint: Use the sound-spelling pattern from the lesson to complete the word.

help.concept: Kreyòl spelling keeps meaningful vowel and sound patterns visible in the written word.
help.hint_1: Focus on the spelling pattern named in the lesson instead of applying English spelling habits.
help.hint_2: Compare the letters and accent marks carefully before choosing your response.

exchange-listen-bonjou.title: Hear the opening
exchange-listen-bonjou.prompt: Listen to the first turn and build what you hear.
exchange-listen-bonjou.hint: Replay the audio, then rebuild exactly what you hear.

help.concept: Listening practice connects the complete written Kreyòl phrase with the phrase you hear.
help.hint_1: Replay the phrase and keep the words in the same order.
help.hint_2: Listen for the whole word or phrase rather than trying to translate each sound into English spelling.

exchange-say-mesi.title: Say thank you
exchange-say-mesi.prompt: Say the familiar Kreyòl word shown: Mèsi.
exchange-say-mesi.hint: Read the Kreyòl target once, then say the whole phrase.

help.concept: Speaking practice checks the transcript of the phrase you say against the authored Kreyòl target.
help.hint_1: Say the complete target phrase clearly at a comfortable pace.
help.hint_2: Use the written Kreyòl as your guide; this activity checks the transcript, not a phoneme-level pronunciation score.

exchange-build-wi-mesi.title: Build a familiar response
exchange-build-wi-mesi.prompt: Arrange the words to make “Yes, thank you.”
exchange-build-wi-mesi.hint: Build the complete Kreyòl phrase in natural order.

help.concept: Sentence building uses the same Kreyòl word order and spelling that appear in the target phrase.
help.hint_1: Start with the phrase you recognize, then place the remaining word or punctuation in its natural position.
help.hint_2: Read the complete result aloud once before checking it.

exchange-write-bonjou.title: Write the opening
exchange-write-bonjou.prompt: Type the Kreyòl greeting used to open the mini exchange.
exchange-write-bonjou.hint: Write the Kreyòl form exactly as it appears in the lesson.

help.concept: Accurate Kreyòl writing preserves the spelling patterns and meaningful accent marks shown in the lesson.
help.hint_1: Write the complete Kreyòl form, including any accent mark that belongs in the word.
help.hint_2: Check the vowel spelling one more time before submitting.

exchange-map.title: Use familiar language in sequence
exchange-map.bodyMarkdown:
A conversation can begin with language you already recognize. For this first mini exchange, keep it deliberately small:

**A:** Bonjou.

**B:** Bonjou.

The purpose is not to learn a large greeting system yet. That comes in the next module. Here you are proving that familiar spelling and sound can survive inside a real turn-taking pattern.

respond-with-known-words.title: Reuse before adding more
respond-with-known-words.bodyMarkdown:
Good beginner practice reuses known language. After hearing a familiar word, respond with a familiar word or phrase instead of reaching for new vocabulary.

You already have **bonjou**, **mèsi**, **wi**, and **non**. Use them accurately. The next module will expand these anchors into fuller social exchanges.

module-one-review.title: Sound, spelling, and use belong together
module-one-review.bodyMarkdown:
Before leaving Module 1, check three habits:

1. You notice spellings such as **è**, **ou**, **an**, **en**, and **on**.
2. You can connect a few written Kreyòl words with what you hear and say.
3. You preserve those spellings when you build or type a response.

You do not need perfect pronunciation or a large vocabulary yet. You need a dependable first map.
